original_question: Establish conditions under which the Cantor-set families arising from the preceding four problems - asymmetric iterated-function-system constructions with K >= 2 maps, constructions with irrational retained end-points, variable-gap middle-interval deletions with parameters (alpha_n) satisfying 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0, and the symmetry-enforced or symmetry-relaxed versions of that variable-gap problem - have a non-empty mutual intersection.
target_in_paper: Section 4, open problem (v) "Common ground": establish conditions under which the families arising in problems (i)-(iv) admit a non-empty mutual intersection.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the intended problem is the last open problem in Section 4, and it correctly ties that problem to the four immediately preceding directions: asymmetric IFS constructions, irrational retained end-points, variable-gap deletions, and the symmetry-enforced versus symmetry-relaxed version of the variable-gap problem. It also correctly preserves the paper’s emphasis on asking for conditions that guarantee a non-empty common intersection of the corresponding Cantor-set families.
missing_details: The paper works with deterministic Cantor sets on the real line, concretely via constructions inside the closed unit interval [0,1]; that ambient setting should be made explicit.
The relevant IFS notion is the affine IFS of Section 2.4: a finite family of affine contractions on [0,1]. If the symbol K is used, it should be defined as the number of maps, with K >= 2.

Problem (v) is about the intersection of families of Cantor sets admitting the respective descriptive realizations from problems (i)-(iv), not about intersection of intervals, end-point sets, or parameter spaces.
Problem (ii) concerns Cantor sets whose retained/surviving intervals have irrational end-points, while still allowing IFS components; that qualifier should be stated explicitly.
Problem (iv) is specifically a refinement of problem (iii): it asks how the solution to the variable-gap deletion problem changes when symmetry is imposed or dropped.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should state the existential content of 'non-empty mutual intersection': there exists at least one deterministic Cantor set belonging simultaneously to all four families.
The paper’s framing is descriptive/set-theoretic: the families are those for which one seeks explicit or recursive set-theoretic formulas, so that descriptive emphasis should be retained.

Your draft imports the alpha_n constraints from problem (iii), but the official target is still problem (v); those hypotheses should appear only as the definition of the third family being intersected, not as a separate main goal.
refined_question: For deterministic Cantor sets C subseteq [0,1], determine conditions under which the intersection of the four Cantor-set families singled out in Section 4(i)-(iv) is nonempty, namely: the family of sets admitting an explicit or recursive set-theoretic description via a finite affine iterated-function system {T_k}_{k=1}^K with K >= 2 whose maps do not preserve bilateral symmetry; the family whose retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing IFS components; the family obtained by variable-gap middle deletions in which, at stage n, the open middle interval of length alpha_n is removed for a sequence (alpha_n)_{n>=1} satisfying 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0; and the symmetry-enforced or symmetry-relaxed versions of that variable-gap construction?
justification: The nearest official formulation is the Section 4 item explicitly labeled "Common ground," which asks for conditions under which the families from the four previous open problems intersect nontrivially. The surrounding context matters: Section 2.4 defines the IFS framework as a finite affine IFS on [0,1], and Section 3 together with Corollary 3.4 explains the motivation by showing that the classical middle-third Cantor set already lies in the intersection of the three families treated in the paper. The generic instruction to prioritize Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 does not apply here, because this paper’s relevant target is not one of those labels but the Section 4 open-problem list. The available HTML rendering drops some inline symbols in item (iii), so the alpha_n hypothesis in your draft is retained as the faithful stand-alone transcription of that third family while keeping the main target fixed on problem (v).
